course.title: The Adventures of Pinocchio
course.learnerRule: A learner completes one selected level per session; Foundation, Core, and Studio are alternatives, not cumulative work.

story.guidingQuestionKo: 두려움보다 사랑이 더 커지는 순간은 언제일까요?
story.synopsisKo: 상어의 배 속에서 제페토를 찾은 피노키오는 지난 여행을 고백하고, 아버지를 등에 업은 채 함께 탈출한다.

editorialPolicy.storyFidelity: The twelve sessions preserve the complete original 36-chapter arc, causal sequence, major choices, consequences, reunions, and ending.
editorialPolicy.foundation: Concrete, speakable sentences with one main action and mostly 6–11 words per line.
editorialPolicy.core: Connected sentences with cause, contrast, and reaction, mostly 10–18 words per line.
editorialPolicy.studio: Literary but performable sentences that preserve narrator wit, suspense, and moral tension.
editorialPolicy.safety: Historic peril and slapstick retain their narrative consequence without added graphic detail.
editorialPolicy.narration: Generate one continuous master per session and level; Watch and Mimic must seek within the same performance.
editorialPolicy.classTime: The story text remains concise; sixty minutes comes from deliberate replay, recording, comparison, retrieval, and sentence reconstruction—not padding the narration.

narration.direction: Hold the darkness and distant candle patiently, let the reunion breathe, perform Pinocchio's long confession with urgency, and make the second escape attempt resolute and luminous.
narration.productionRule: Generate one continuous master per session and level; Watch and Mimic seek within that exact same master.

livingStorybook.artBrief: A vast dark Shark interior leads from Tunny and a distant candle to Geppetto's tiny table, swallowed ship supplies, throat, moonlit open mouth, tongue road, sneeze setback, and final leap into the sea.

beats.summaryKo: 완전한 어둠 속에서 작은 촛불을 발견한다.
두 해 동안 갇힌 아버지와 마침내 만난다.
제페토가 배의 식량으로 버틴 사연을 말한다.
마지막 촛불이 꺼지기 전에 나가기로 한다.
두 번째 시도에서 함께 바다로 뛰어든다.

lines.text: Pinocchio followed a tiny light through the darkness.
An old man sat beside the last candle.
The old man was his father, Geppetto.
Father and son hugged, laughed, and cried.
Pinocchio told Geppetto about his long journey.
Geppetto described the storm and the Terrible Shark.
He had lived inside it for two years.
Food from a swallowed ship kept him alive.
Now the supplies and final candle were ending.
Pinocchio said they must escape immediately.
Geppetto could not swim, but Pinocchio could.
The old Shark slept with its mouth open.
A sudden sneeze ruined their first escape.
Pinocchio took Geppetto's hand and tried again.
Geppetto climbed securely onto his son's back.
Together they jumped and swam into moonlight.

lines.text: Pinocchio left the Tunny and followed a tiny light through the darkness.
At a small table, an old man ate beside his final candle.
The white-haired prisoner was Geppetto, the father Pinocchio had searched for.
They embraced in disbelief, laughing and crying at the same time.
Pinocchio poured out the entire story of his mistakes and misfortunes.
Geppetto explained how the storm and Terrible Shark had swallowed him.
He had survived inside the monster for two long years.
Supplies from a swallowed merchant ship had provided food, candles, and matches.
Now the food was gone, and the candle on the table was the last.
Pinocchio insisted that they attempt an escape before darkness returned.
Although Geppetto could not swim, Pinocchio promised to carry him.
The ancient Shark's asthma forced it to sleep with its mouth open.
Their first attempt failed when a sudden sneeze threw them backward.
Pinocchio refused despair, took his father's hand, and climbed again.
At the final row of teeth, Geppetto climbed onto his son's back.
Pinocchio leaped into the moonlit water and began carrying them home.

lines.text: Leaving the resigned Tunny behind, Pinocchio followed a faint light through the vast darkness of the Shark.
The glow came from a final candle beside a tiny table where a white-haired old man ate live fish.
Recognition arrived almost too powerfully for speech: the prisoner was Geppetto, still waiting after two years.
Father and son embraced with the confused laughter and tears of people who had imagined each other lost.
Pinocchio released the entire journey in one breathless confession, naming temptations, lies, punishments, helpers, and regret.
Geppetto answered with his own story of the storm, the overturned boat, and the monster that swallowed him.
A merchant ship had also disappeared into the Shark, leaving enough supplies to sustain one man in darkness.
Those provisions had lasted two years, but now both the cupboard and the final candle were nearly empty.
Pinocchio immediately proposed escaping through the mouth, treating action as responsibility rather than impulse.
Geppetto admitted that he could not swim and doubted that a small marionette could carry him.
His son answered that they should test courage together rather than wait separately for the end.
Because age and asthma forced the Shark to sleep with its mouth open, moonlight marked a possible route.
A sudden sneeze destroyed their first attempt and sent them sliding back into darkness without the candle.
Pinocchio refused the language of defeat, found his father's hand, and led the climb a second time.
Beyond the tongue and three rows of teeth, Geppetto settled his weight onto the wooden shoulders.
Pinocchio leaped into the calm moonlit sea, finally using his strength to carry the father who had carried him.
